newsitem.title: ZAIRE: Zaire rebels say Kenya summit pointless.
newsitem.headline: Zaire rebels say Kenya summit pointless.

text.p: A Zairean rebel spokesman said on Thursday that nothing of value could come from a planned peace summit in Kenya from which rebel leader Laurent Kabila and Rwanda and Uganda have been excluded.

Rebel justice minister, Mwenze Kongolo, told Reuters in Kindu, the latest major town to fall to the rebels, that Kenyan President Daniel arap Moi was biased in favour of Zairean President Mobutu Sese Seko.
"We have always said clearly that nothing could come out of a summit in Nairobi. Moi is part of the conflict because he has always been such a close ally of Mobutu Sese Seko," he said.
Kenya's Foreign Ministry said Mobutu, South Africa's President Nelson Mandela and five other African heads of state had been invited to a one-day summit on the civil war on March 19.
The rebel Alliance of Democratic Forces for the Liberation (ADFL) of Congo has captured a huge chunk of eastern Zaire since launching the rebellion in October to end Mobutu's 31 year rule.
Rebel fighters are poised to attack Kisangani, eastern Zaire's main city and the base for an unsuccsesful government counter-offensive.
The rebels say a ceasefire can only come after negotiations with Mobutu to discuss his own departure from power. Zaire has ruled out such a face-to-face meeting.
Zaire accuses Uganda, Rwanda and Burundi of invading in support of the rebels. All three reject the charge.

Mwenze rejected French charges that Ugandan troops have fought in Zaire on behalf of the rebels. "Where are these supposed Ugandans? I don't see them in Kindu and I've not seen a single Ugandan soldier in the areas liberated by the Alliance."
